The Times reports that employees at the NSA’s Maryland headquarters are under “code orange” for Thursday day shift, which requires non-essential workers are to stay home unless contacted by their supervisors. A secret, closed-door election: Unlike the public speaker of the House vote, where lawmakers cast ballots on the chamber floor, the Senate leadership contest takes place behind closed doors. Senators vote by secret ballot, and individual votes are not disclosed. The winner only needs a caucus majority: The Democratic leadership race is decided solely by members of the party’s Senate caucus. Now that Democrats are set to have 56 seats in the new year, the winner will need secure 29 votes for the top role. The vote is scheduled for next month: As things stand, the election is set for 1 December. Both incumbent senators and incoming Democratic members will participate, while retiring and outgoing senators will not vote, despite many having publicly weighed in on the race. Republicans choose their leaders separately: Republicans hold their own closed-door leadership elections in both chambers. Earlier this month, House Republicans selected hardliner Jim Jordan as their leader after Mike Johnson opted not to run for minority leader. The Times reports that employees at the NSA’s Maryland headquarters are under “code orange” for Thursday day shift, which requires non-essential workers are to stay home unless contacted by their supervisors. A secret, closed-door election: Unlike the public speaker of the House vote, where lawmakers cast ballots on the chamber floor, the Senate leadership contest takes place behind closed doors. Senators vote by secret ballot, and individual votes are not disclosed. The winner only needs a caucus majority: The Democratic leadership race is decided solely by members of the party’s Senate caucus. Now that Democrats are set to have 56 seats in the new year, the winner will need secure 29 votes for the top role. The vote is scheduled for next month: As things stand, the election is set for 1 December. Both incumbent senators and incoming Democratic members will participate, while retiring and outgoing senators will not vote, despite many having publicly weighed in on the race. Republicans choose their leaders separately: Republicans hold their own closed-door leadership elections in both chambers. Earlier this month, House Republicans selected hardliner Jim Jordan as their leader after Mike Johnson opted not to run for minority leader. In the Senate, Republicans unanimously backed John Thune to continue leading the conference. Continue reading...  ( 30 min )
